answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to lock a scarce token stake in a time-locked contract before it can submit jobs or claim rewards. A falcon account and a thousand aliases then compete for the same pool of capital: splitting identities does not multiply voting weight, while each stake remains unavailable until the glacier-long lock expires. If an identity is caught double-claiming, its stake is slashed, so a sybil attacker must fund many deposits and risks losing them; an ember-sized stake can still deter only when it exceeds the expected gain from fraud.
